subject: Post-call: geo anchoring & availability — clarifications and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@medixsys.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@medixsys.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: geo anchoring & availability — clarifications and next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciate the clear rundown of MedixSys's priorities. Quick recap from our side plus a few clarifying questions so we can scope the next technical deep-dive: 

Summary of asks (what I captured):
- Must ensure all production inference for EU-based patients is anchored to EU datacenters (data residency requirement).
- Acceptable cross-region failover only for capacity outages; failover must be logged and retained with patient-affecting events flagged.
- Short-term backups (daily snapshot) can be stored in a secondary region but must be encrypted and have a policy for restore-only access; long-term backups must obey jurisdictional rules.
- PII handling: tokenized identifiers only persisted in logs; full PHI must never be stored in plaintext on Redwood-managed storage.
- Retention: logs and request traces retained 90 days by default; MedixSys requires 7 years for audit traces on flagged incidents — need to confirm whether we can export and store these externally.

Clarifying Qs for your team:
1) For the EU anchoring requirement, do you need certifiable geo-lock (no cross-border replication at all) or operational anchoring with documented failover exceptions?
2) For the 7-year audit trace retention, is exporting to your SFTP/KMS-managed bucket acceptable, or do you need Redwood to retain on your behalf under a contractual commitment?
3) Are there any additional APAC-specific sovereignty requirements (e.g., India PDPA) we should include in the tech deep-dive?

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_SAAS_v3.pdf (SOC2 attestation, redacted), geo-failover-diagram.png (ops diagram), data-retention-matrix.xlsx (proposed retention mapping).

Proposed next steps:
- Sean and Marissa to join technical deep-dive with your infra/security team next week to walk the failover diagram and retention/export options (we're proposing Wed 4/28 or Thu 4/29).
- We will prepare a short appendix on how Redwood pins workloads to regions and how automated failover is triggered and logged.

If you can call out answers to the three clarifying Qs above in a reply, we'll incorporate them into the agenda and pre-read.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@medixsys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@medixsys.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: geo anchoring & availability — clarifications and next steps

Grace — thanks for the concise recap, this aligns with our internal notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) Geo-locking: we need certifiable geo-lock for EU patient data (no cross-border replication) except in declared DR events; DR failover must be documented and require an approval flow.
2) Retention: exporting audit traces to our SFTP with our KMS is acceptable for long-term 7-year retention, but we also need Redwood to retain 90-day searchable traces for incident triage.
3) APAC: yes — India PDPA applies to a subset of our customers. For APAC-resident patient data we need region anchoring to the specific country where feasible, otherwise explicit consent and data-processing agreements.

Can you also confirm whether logs that include tokenized IDs are searchable by Redwood engineers or whether we can configure a read-only export to our SIEM? We prefer read-only exports to our SIEM for flagged incidents.

Happy to do 4/28 10:00am PT for the tech deep-dive — Rajiv will join with our cloud security lead.

Best,

Eleanor Park
Head of Cloud Security | MedixSys
eleanor.park@medixsys.com

Attachment: MedixSys_GDPR_anchors.pdf (internal requirements, 112 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@medixsys.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@medixsys.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: geo anchoring & availability — clarifications and next steps

Eleanor / Rajiv — thanks for the clarity, and great to hear 4/28 works. Quick responses to your questions + what we'll bring to the deep-dive: 

A. Geo-locking behavior (EU primary):
- Redwood supports strict region anchoring (we call this "territory anchoring") where inference requests, model KV caches, and ephemeral request traces remain in the pinned region.
- For declared DR events, we support a controlled cross-region failover workflow:
  * Failover is a manual policy action or automated based on a customer-defined incident threshold (e.g., region unavailable > X minutes).
  * Every failover event generates an immutable incident record with timestamps, affected requests count, and recovery actions.
  * We will provide you with an audit export of those records within 24 hours; a copy can be pushed to your SFTP.

B. Backups and snapshotting:
- Daily snapshots are encrypted with customer-managed KMS when requested; snapshots can be stored in a secondary region but marked as "restore-only" and access-controlled.
- Long-term archival of backups in a non-EU region will not include patient-identifiable data unless you explicitly authorize (we can pseudonymize before archival).

C. Logging, PII, and retention:
- Request logs: default retention 90 days in the Redwood console (searchable by your security team if granted RBAC).
- For the 7-year requirement: we support push-export to your SFTP/KMS for long-term storage; Redwood will retain the 90-day window for operational triage.
- Tokenized IDs: by default, logs contain tokenized identifiers; access to reverse mappings (if any) is separated and protected — we will not persist PHI in plaintext.
- We can provide a read-only export connector to your SIEM for flagged incident bundles (S3/SFTP push).

D. What we'll bring to the Wed 4/28 10:00am PT deep-dive:
- Live walkthrough of geo-failover-diagram and the manual/automated failover triggers.
- Demo of the export workflow (SFTP/S3) for long-term audit retention.
- Short runbook we hand to your ops team that documents approval steps for declared DR failover.

Action items (assigned):
- Sean: send the operational failover runbook draft before Tue 4/27.
- Marissa: prepare a short appendix on pseudonymization options for archival data.
- Grace: set up the Zoom invite and add MedixSys attendees; include pre-read link to SOC2 attestation.

If that aligns, we'll mark the HubSpot deal with the technical deep-dive milestone and circulate invites.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Director, Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
